sections.h2: Augusta County and its independent cities
sections.html:
Augusta County sits in the Shenandoah Valley on the western side of Virginia. At 971 square miles it is one of the largest counties in the state, and it had 77,487 residents in the 2020 census. Craigsville and Grottoes are the two towns inside it, and the larger communities include Stuarts Draft, Fishersville and Verona.

The county wraps around the independent cities of Staunton and Waynesboro, and those cities are not part of it. For a seller that split decides who sends the bill. A house with a Staunton or Waynesboro mailing address may be taxed by the city, while a house just outside the line is taxed by Augusta County. The parcel's location settles it, not the community name on an envelope, so check the county's online assessment records or call the offices before you assume.

Taxes are due in equal installments on June 5 and December 5. If a date falls on a weekend, the due date moves to the following Monday, and you may pay the full annual amount in June. Bills can be viewed and paid on the county's e-Treasurer site.

InstallmentDue dateIf paid late
First halfJune 510 percent penalty plus 10 percent yearly interest
Second halfDecember 510 percent penalty plus 10 percent yearly interest
Full year in one paymentJuneNo second bill

The penalty applies to the unpaid balance, and interest runs on what remains unpaid. The state's share of personal property tax is excluded from the interest.

sections.h2: When Augusta County waives a late charge
sections.html:
Taxpayers are responsible for knowing the due dates. If no bill arrives, contact the taxing office before the due date to arrange payment. Some reasons never waive the charge: not knowing the due date, not getting a bill, a bill mailed to the wrong address, an incorrect bill, and wrong information from county staff.

The charge may be waived in narrower cases.

  • A medically determinable physical or mental impairment on the due date, with payment within 30 days.
  • The Commissioner of the Revenue abates the tax or certifies a clerical error by that office.
  • The late payment was caused solely by the Treasurer or the Commissioner of the Revenue.

If you cannot pay in full, ask the Treasurer's Office about a payment plan at (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us. A plan leaves the penalty in place and interest keeps running.

The Board of Supervisors sets the rate, and the county's 2024 rate was $0.52 per $100 of assessed value. The Real Estate Assessor's Office assesses property as of January 1. Check your current bill for the rate that applies now.

Augusta reassesses on a five-year cycle. The 2024 reassessment started in September 2022, with notices mailed in February 2024, and the county hired Wampler-Eanes Appraisal Group and divided the county into about 96 neighborhoods. Staff visited accessible properties to check records and update property cards and photos.

The county's analysis of 2023 residential sales found 680 sales with a median increase of 58.3 percent over the old assessment. Increases were highest in Beverly Manor at 69.5 percent and North River at 68.8 percent, and lowest in Craigsville at 33.7 percent, a figure based on only three sales.

Many owners saw a sharp rise in 2024. Your new value is a county estimate, not a sale price, so weigh it against what a buyer would actually pay.

The county describes three steps: an informal hearing with the assessor, the Board of Equalization, then Circuit Court. Informal appeals could be made by Zoom, phone, email, mail or in person.

  • Common reasons: a value that seems too high or too low, market value disparities, changes in condition, comparable sales and clerical errors.
  • Deadlines vary by notice, so use the dates printed on yours.

Under Virginia Code section 58.1-3381 the board can increase, decrease or affirm an assessment, and an owner must be notified before an increase. In court, section 58.1-3984 treats the assessor's value as correct and puts the burden on the owner to rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence.

Unpaid tax stays with the property. Virginia Code section 58.1-3340 gives real estate a tax lien that ranks ahead of other liens until paid, and sale proceeds are applied to the tax. How the current year is split between buyer and seller is set by the contract.

On the deed, the grantor tax under section 58.1-802 is 50 cents for each $500 and is paid by the seller unless the parties agree otherwise. The state recordation tax under section 58.1-801 is 25 cents per $100. Section 58.1-3916 caps a locality's penalty at 10 percent of the tax past due or $10, whichever is greater, and interest at 10 percent a year, which matches what Augusta County charges.

Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before closing and keep the receipt for your title company. We buy as is, so an open balance is something we can work through with you.

sections.h2: What to do before you list
sections.html:
Pull up the parcel on the county's assessment records and confirm which locality bills it. Look at the 2024 value and compare it with recent sales near you. If you plan to sell soon, call the Treasurer for the balance on both installments so nothing surprises you at the table.

A seller whose job or a relative's care moves them out of the area can sell without waiting on a long financing process. We buy houses as they are.

faqs.q: Are Staunton and Waynesboro part of Augusta County?
faqs.a: No. They are independent cities that Augusta County surrounds. A house inside either city is generally handled by the city, so check which office bills you.

faqs.q: When are Augusta County property taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. A due date on a weekend moves to the following Monday.

faqs.q: What is the late penalty in Augusta County?
faqs.a: A 10 percent penalty on the unpaid balance and 10 percent annual interest. A payment plan does not remove either charge.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about a payment plan?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's Office at (540) 245-5660 or treasurer@co.augusta.va.us.

faqs.q: How many years between Augusta County reassessments?
faqs.a: Five. The latest reassessment took effect in 2024.
